analyst_view.overall: Early view: Granada have won five league games in a row under Pacheta but have not played in the league since 1 November because their home game with Tenerife was postponed. Las Palmas changed coach in late October; one report says Albert Sánchez won his debut 3-2 at Oviedo, and Jesé (four goals) has just renewed. Las Palmas also had a round-13 home game against Eldense that is not yet in these numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Granada's winning run has been built on narrow scores, with clean sheets in three of the five, and none of the last five meetings between these clubs produced more than three goals. Las Palmas's new coach is also still settling his side.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners and I keep it there. Granada are happy without the ball (Eldense had 59 per cent of it against them last time out), so their 5.3 may be a little high, but Las Palmas should get more than 3.9 if they have the ball. The total looks about right.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and I see no clear push either way. Las Palmas have collected cards steadily (32 yellows and two reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), which the site already reflects in their 3.2, and Granada's 1.9 fits a side that sits off the ball and wins narrowly.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots, with Granada expected to take 14.9. I lean lower: Granada were outshot 13-8 at Eldense and still won, so their results come from efficiency rather than volume. Two weeks without a league game may also blunt their sharpness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I lean lower: Rubén Alcaraz's winner at Elda was Granada's first shot on target of the second half, and recent meetings between these sides have been short of chances.
